subject: Re: Compact retain + insights SKU smoothing
messages:
From: Alex Tully <alex.tully@brightline.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@brightline.ai>
Date: 2027-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Compact retain + insights SKU — initial pricing tolerance

Hi Michael / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Brightline is excited about Redwood's low-latency inference and the visibility suite — particularly the compact retain window + advanced dashboards for our analytics team. Procurement asked me to kick off pricing alignment so we can move to internal approval. A few constraints on our side: 

- We need a flat predictable SKU for retain (30-day active KV + 90-day archival) rather than per-GB month-by-month; finance prefers slab-style billing.
- We can commit to a 12-month reserved commit for inference tokens but would like observability add-ons to be ring-fenced as an annual per-seat or per-slab credit model.
- Targeted total TCV for year 1 is ~$650k.

Can you share an example packaging that smooths observability costs into the commit (or show concession paths)? Also, procurement requested a short SOW and an example invoice line items spreadsheet.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow if helpful.

Alex
Head of Partnerships
Brightline AI

Attachments: none
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tully <alex.tully@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact retain + insights SKU — initial pricing tolerance

Alex — thanks for the detail and the timeframe. Love the idea of smoothing into the commit; we do that often for customers who want predictable OPEX. High-level options we can offer: 

1) Slab-included: Observability (30-day retain / 90-day archival) bundled as a per-seat slab that is amortized across the annual commit. This reduces spike exposure but is less granular.
2) Credit pool: Add-ons consumed from an annual credit pool tied to the commit (recommended if you expect heavy dashboard/trace spikes in Q4).
3) Hybrid: Baseline slab for core dashboards + credit buffer for ephemeral spikes.

I'll attach a rough SOW template and a pricing worksheet showing these three constructs and an example concession path that hits ~650k TCV (assuming a 12-month commit and a modest observability inclusion). Marissa / Ben — can you review the worksheet and flag if we can compress further on seat pricing for the dashboards?

I can join procurement call if needed — suggest a 30-min sync this Thursday (9/2).

Best,
Michael Grant
Sr. Director, GTM — Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_spreadsheet_v3.xlsx (xlsx), SOW_template.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact retain + insights SKU — initial pricing tolerance

Looping in a couple quick numbers — ran this with finance: if we do a hybrid (baseline slab + 20% credit buffer) and push 12-month commit, we can offer a 10% commercial concession on the observability add-ons (applied as an up-front credit) and maintain margin. That gets close to Brightline's 650k TCV, assuming inference unit pricing is standard.

Two negotiation levers:
- Increase commit by 10% to bring TCV into discount band (we can then add retention slab at no additional cost).
- Or keep commit flat; we apply a one-time observability credit and reduce per-seat dashboard price (smaller concession).

I'll prepare the revised worksheet with the concession paths.

— Ben
Head of Sales Strategy
From: Alex Tully <alex.tully@brightline.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procure@brightline.ai>
Date: 2027-09-01T11:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact retain + insights SKU — initial pricing tolerance

Thanks Michael / Ben. Procurement ran two scenarios during our finance huddle: 

A) Keep to 650k TCV. Procurement prefers smaller monthly payments and a fixed observability slab in the commit so our analysts have predictable quotas.
B) Increase to ~715k (10% bump) if Redwood will include the 30-day retain slab and provide a 15% observability credit in year one.

Their preference is A but they asked if Redwood can do A + a pilot concession (i.e., keep commit at 650k, but Redwood applies a one-time pilot credit to be reconciled in Q1 if usage materially exceeds baseline). Could you outline that pilot-concession mechanism and the milestones that trigger reconciliation? We also need a slightly updated SOW (scope: production inference, dedicated KV retention configuration, access to advanced dashboards for 10 analysts).

Best,
Alex

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Tully <alex.tully@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-02T17:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact retain + insights SKU — initial pricing tolerance

Alex — appreciate the clear options. Attached is a short, versioned SOW (Brightline_SOW_v2.pdf) that matches Scenario A with an appended pilot concession clause. Key points of the concession clause: 

- Pilot credit: one-time observability credit equal to 12% of the observability line (applied in month 1).
- Usage reconciliation: if observability consumption > 130% of the forecasted baseline during the first 90 days, reconciliation occurs and additional credits/charges are handled via an agreed runbook.
- Milestones: production ingestion (M1), dashboard enablement for 10 analysts (M2), and Q1 usage review (M3). Reconciliation actions require sign-off from both sides (Brightline procurement + Redwood finance).

Irene — can you confirm the runbook language and the exact telemetry metrics we should use for reconciliation?

If that reads OK, Alex — we'd like signature on the SOW and the order form. I also attached the revised pricing_spreadsheet_v3.xlsx with the Scenario A numbers and the pilot credit line. Happy to take a 30-minute procurement call tomorrow to walk through the reconciliation mechanics.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Sr. Director, GTM — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Brightline_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf), pricing_spreadsheet_v3.xlsx (xlsx)
